claims.text: Untreated NbMoCrTi-based refractory high-entropy alloys suffer from rapid oxidation and oxide spallation under extreme-temperature conditions.
The alloy composition will be modified by adding approximately 5 at% Al.
Adding approximately 5 at% Al to the refractory alloy will produce an alumina scale in situ.
The alumina scale formed after Al addition will be continuous and adherent.
The protective alumina scale will be slow-growing.
Aluminum in the modified alloy will preferentially oxidize to alumina.
The alumina layer will lower oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy.
Lower oxygen diffusion through the alumina layer will reduce further oxidation.
Formation of the alumina layer will reduce oxide-scale spallation.
The Al-added alloy will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than the untreated alloy.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the Al-added alloy will show significantly lower weight gain and diminished oxide spallation after exposure at 1100°C in 5% O2 with Ar balance for 100 hours.
The untreated alloy will undergo rapid oxidation, substantial weight gain, and oxide-scale degradation at 1100°C in 5% O2 over 100 hours.
The oxidation-resistance improvement is expected at approximately 1100°C, about 5% O2, and 100 hours of exposure.
At lower temperatures or different oxygen levels, the benefit of alumina-scale formation may be less pronounced.
Processing and microstructural variability could affect alumina-scale formation and adhesion.
